title: Disclosure of Sensitive Registration Data During Transmission
description: Parent registration data (email, password, name, govt ID, six-digit code) transmitted from ExternalEntity EE1 to Process P1 may be intercepted or disclosed to unauthorized parties during the flow.
assumptions: Data is transmitted over network without adequate encryption or authentication controls.
uncertainty_note: Using D.1.1 as generic disclosure node; exact LINDDUN Pro node may vary by implementation.

title: Identification of Parent User via Registration Data
description: Govt ID and email address in registration flow can be used to identify the parent user, potentially enabling profiling or tracking across systems.
assumptions: Govt ID and email are unique identifiers that can be correlated with other data sources.
uncertainty_note: I.1.1 is a generic identification node; specific context may require different node.

title: Usurpation/Impersonation via Registration Credentials
description: Password and govt ID combination enables potential identity theft or account takeover, allowing unauthorized access to parent account.
assumptions: Credentials are stored or transmitted without adequate protection against interception or replay attacks.
uncertainty_note: U.1.1 is a generic usurpation node; exact node may depend on specific threat-tree structure.

title: Disclosure of Registration Data by Authentication Service
description: Authentication Service P1 may disclose parent registration data (email, password, name, govt ID) to unauthorized internal or external systems.
assumptions: P1 lacks proper access controls, audit logging, or data minimization practices.
uncertainty_note: D.1.1 is a generic disclosure node; specific implementation details may affect threat assessment.

title: Alteration of Registration Data by Authentication Service
description: Authentication Service P1 may alter parent registration data (email, password, govt ID) during processing, leading to data integrity violations.
assumptions: P1 lacks input validation, integrity checks, or tamper detection mechanisms.
uncertainty_note: Dd.1.1 is a generic data alteration node; actual risk depends on P1's security controls.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of parent account data during storage
description: Parent account personal data stored in MongoDB users collection may be disclosed to unauthorized parties through inadequate access controls or improper authentication mechanisms in the Authentication Service.
assumptions: Authentication Service has access to MongoDB users collection and stores parent account data
uncertainty_note: Using Dd.1.1 as it represents explicit disclosure through the storage process

title: Data alteration of parent account information
description: Parent account data stored in MongoDB users collection could be modified by unauthorized actors or through system vulnerabilities, leading to data integrity issues.
assumptions: MongoDB users collection is accessible and parent account data is sensitive
uncertainty_note: D.1.1 represents data alteration threat at the process level

title: Data disclosure from MongoDB users collection
description: MongoDB users collection storing parent account data may expose personal information to unauthorized access through insufficient access controls or improper data handling.
assumptions: MongoDB users collection contains parent account personal data
uncertainty_note: Dd.1.1 applies to data disclosure from data store perspective

title: User Identifiability via JWT Token
description: The JWT token transmitted from the Authentication Service to the Parent User contains user data that could identify the individual. If the JWT is intercepted or improperly handled, it could reveal personally identifiable information.
assumptions: JWT contains user-identifying information; Parent User has access to the JWT
uncertainty_note: Tree node I.1.1 is a standard LINDDUN Pro node for identifiability threats at source/flow/destination

title: Linkability of User Data Across Systems
description: The JWT and user data sent to the Parent User could be linked to other data sources or systems, enabling correlation of user activities across different contexts.
assumptions: Parent User or third parties could correlate this data with other datasets
uncertainty_note: Tree node L.1.1 is a standard LINDDUN Pro node for linkability threats

title: User Usurpation via JWT Token
description: The JWT token could be stolen or misused by unauthorized parties to impersonate the authenticated user, leading to unauthorized access or actions on behalf of the user.
assumptions: JWT tokens are transmitted over potentially insecure channels; Parent User system may not validate token integrity
uncertainty_note: Tree node U.1.1 is a standard LINDDUN Pro node for usurpation threats

title: Linkability of JWT and child profiles across services
description: The JWT token and child profile data transmitted from the Authentication Service could be linked to identify the child user across different services or contexts, potentially enabling tracking of the child's activities and preferences.
assumptions: Assumes the JWT and profile data contain sufficient identifying information to enable cross-service correlation.
uncertainty_note: Tree node L.1.1 is a standard LINDDUN Pro node for linkability at source/flow/destination; confidence in this specific node choice is moderate.

title: Identification of child user through authentication data
description: The Authentication Service processes and transmits data that could be used to identify the child user, including JWT tokens and profile information that may contain personally identifiable information.
assumptions: Assumes the JWT and profile data contain or can be combined to form identifying information about the child.
uncertainty_note: Tree node I.1.1 is a standard LINDDUN Pro node for identification at source/flow/destination.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child profile data
description: The child user (ExternalEntity) may receive or store the JWT and profile data in ways that could lead to unauthorized disclosure to third parties, either through insecure storage or sharing.
assumptions: Assumes the child user or their devices may not have adequate security controls for storing sensitive profile data.
uncertainty_note: Tree node D.1.1 is a standard LINDDUN Pro node for disclosure at destination; the severity is high due to the sensitive nature of child profile data.

title: Usurpation of child user identity through JWT token
description: An attacker who obtains the JWT token could potentially impersonate the child user, gaining unauthorized access to services or systems that trust the authentication service.
assumptions: Assumes JWT tokens are not properly secured or are transmitted over channels vulnerable to interception.
uncertainty_note: Tree node U.1.1 is a standard LINDDUN Pro node for usurpation at source/flow/destination; this is a critical threat for authentication flows.

title: Linking of child profile data across systems
description: The government ID combined with name, DOB, and gender creates a unique identifier that could be used to link this child's profile data to other databases, external systems, or third-party records, potentially revealing additional information about the child or family.
assumptions: External systems or databases exist that could receive or access this linked data
uncertainty_note: Using L.1.1 as a reasonable node for linking threats; context suggests this applies to ExternalEntity->Process flows

title: Direct identification of child via government ID
description: The government ID is a direct personal identifier that enables unambiguous identification of the child. This creates a privacy risk where the child can be uniquely identified from the profile data.
assumptions: Government ID is a unique identifier for the child
uncertainty_note: I.1.1 is a standard identification threat node; government ID is clearly a direct identifier

title: Unauthorized disclosure of sensitive child profile data
description: The process may disclose sensitive personal data (name, DOB, gender, government ID) to unauthorized parties through improper access controls, data breaches, or insecure transmission channels.
assumptions: Process P3 has access to the data and may transmit it to other systems
uncertainty_note: D.1.1 is a standard disclosure threat node; applies to Process->ExternalEntity or Process->DataStore flows

title: Non-compliance with child data protection regulations
description: Collection and processing of child profile data including government ID may violate regulations such as COPPA, GDPR-K, or other child privacy laws if proper consent, age verification, and data minimization are not implemented.
assumptions: Regulatory requirements exist for child data processing
uncertainty_note: Nc.1.1 is a standard non-compliance node; child data has heightened regulatory requirements

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child profile data to third parties
description: Child profile data stored in MongoDB could be disclosed to unauthorized third parties through improper access controls, data breaches, or unintended data sharing mechanisms.
assumptions: Child profile data contains sensitive personal information that requires strict access controls and encryption.
uncertainty_note: Using Dd.1.1 as a general disclosure node; specific MongoDB access control configurations not known.

title: Linkability of video search results to user identity
description: Video search results and user interactions (likes, comments) may be linked to specific users through their search history, profile data, or account identifiers, enabling tracking of user behavior across sessions.
assumptions: System logs search queries and user interactions with identifiable information

title: Identifiability through video content and comments
description: Video content, search queries, and user comments may contain personally identifiable information or context that allows identification of the user to third parties or unauthorized observers.
assumptions: Video content or comments may reveal user identity, location, or personal details

title: Unauthorized disclosure of video content and interactions
description: Video content, search history, likes, and comments may be disclosed to unauthorized parties through system vulnerabilities, improper access controls, or data breaches.
assumptions: Video data and user interactions are stored and transmitted without adequate protection

title: Improper personal data management for video content
description: Video content and user interaction data may be managed in non-compliant ways, including inadequate retention policies, improper consent handling, or failure to meet privacy regulations.
assumptions: Data management practices may not align with applicable privacy laws and regulations
uncertainty_note: Context [5] confirms Nc.2 applies to improper personal data management risks

title: Identifying information in video metadata
description: Video metadata stored in MongoDB may contain personally identifiable information such as names, locations, timestamps, or other identifying details about individuals captured in the videos.
assumptions: Video metadata includes fields that can identify individuals
uncertainty_note: Using tree node I.1.2 from retrieved context which specifically addresses identified information in metadata

title: Implicit data disclosure through video metadata
description: Video metadata may implicitly disclose personal data through contextual information (e.g., timestamps, locations, device identifiers) even if explicit PII is not stored. This represents avoidable disclosure of personal data.
assumptions: Metadata contains contextual information that can be used to identify individuals
uncertainty_note: Tree node Dd.1.1 inferred from context about data disclosure; implicit disclosure through metadata is a known pattern

title: Linkability of video metadata across systems
description: Video metadata stored in MongoDB could be linked with other data sources (e.g., user accounts, access logs) to create a comprehensive profile of individuals, potentially revealing more than intended.
assumptions: Video metadata can be correlated with other data sources
uncertainty_note: Linkability threat is common in video management systems; tree node L.1.1 represents linkability of metadata

title: Lack of anonymization in video metadata
description: Video metadata may not be properly anonymized or pseudonymized before storage, leaving personally identifiable information exposed in the MongoDB collection.
assumptions: Anonymization is not applied to video metadata
uncertainty_note: Nr.1.1 represents lack of anonymization; severity depends on actual anonymization practices

title: Implicit disclosure of child search and watch history
description: Child search and watch history stored in MongoDB childprofiles collection may be implicitly disclosed through metadata, access logs, or derived data patterns that reveal sensitive information about the child's interests, location, or online behavior without explicit consent.
assumptions: Data is accessible to authorized personnel or systems that could extract or infer sensitive information from stored history.
uncertainty_note: Tree node Dd.1.1 is a general data disclosure node; specific MongoDB access controls not fully known.

title: Identifiability of child through search/watch history
description: Stored child search and watch history may contain personally identifiable information or patterns that could identify the child or their guardians, especially when combined with other data sources.
assumptions: Search queries and watch history contain or can be correlated with identifying information about the child or family.
uncertainty_note: Specific data fields in childprofiles collection not fully documented.

title: Linkability of child data across systems
description: Child search and watch history stored in MongoDB could be linked with other data sources (e.g., user accounts, device IDs, location data) to create comprehensive profiles of the child or family.
assumptions: Other data sources exist that could be correlated with this child profile data.
uncertainty_note: External data sources and correlation mechanisms not fully known.

title: Explicit disclosure of child profile data during management
description: Child Profile Management process may intentionally transfer child search and watch history to third parties (e.g., analytics, marketing, or partner services) without adequate consent or necessity justification.
assumptions: Process includes data sharing functionality or integration with external systems.
uncertainty_note: Specific data sharing mechanisms and third-party recipients not documented.

title: Usurpation of child profile management
description: Unauthorized actors may impersonate children or guardians to access or modify child search and watch history, potentially exploiting weak authentication or session management.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms exist but may be vulnerable to impersonation attacks.
uncertainty_note: Specific authentication controls not documented.

title: Video data linkability to individuals
description: Video upload data can be linked to specific individuals through facial features, context, or metadata, enabling tracking across systems and time.
assumptions: Video data contains biometric and contextual information that can be associated with identifiable persons.

title: Direct identification from video content
description: Video data inherently contains visual information that can directly identify individuals, including faces, voices, and contextual details.
assumptions: Video content is processed and stored in a manner that preserves identifiable features.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of video data
description: Video data may be disclosed to unauthorized parties through system vulnerabilities, improper access controls, or data breaches during upload, storage, or processing.
assumptions: Video data is accessible to system components and potentially exposed through security failures.

title: Identity usurpation via video data
description: Video data can be used to impersonate individuals, assuming their identity for unauthorized access or fraudulent activities.
assumptions: Video data can be extracted, manipulated, or used to create synthetic representations of individuals.

title: Non-compliance with video data privacy regulations
description: Video data handling may violate GDPR, biometric data regulations, or other privacy laws requiring consent, purpose limitation, and data minimization.
assumptions: Video data is classified as biometric or special category data under applicable regulations.

title: Video stream linkable to child identity
description: The video stream from the Video Management Service to the child user could be linked to the child's identity through metadata, timestamps, or contextual information, enabling correlation with other personal data.
assumptions: Video metadata or contextual data is available and accessible

title: Video content reveals identifiable information
description: The video content itself may contain identifiable information about the child or other individuals (e.g., faces, locations, activities) that could be used to identify them without explicit consent.
assumptions: Video content contains visual or contextual identifiers

title: Unauthorized disclosure of video stream
description: The video stream could be intercepted, recorded, or shared with unauthorized third parties during transmission, leading to privacy violations.
assumptions: Transmission channel is not fully secured or monitoring is possible

title: Non-compliance with children's data protection regulations
description: Streaming video of a child may violate GDPR, COPPA, or other regulations regarding processing of children's personal data, particularly if consent mechanisms are inadequate.
assumptions: Regulatory requirements apply to video data of minors
uncertainty_note: Nc.2 citation from context [5] is approximate for this specific regulatory context

title: Unnecessary child browsing data disclosure to AI engine
description: Child browsing data is transferred from MongoDB collection to AI Recommendation Engine. This represents explicit data disclosure of sensitive personal data about children. The minimality principle is violated if the AI engine requires more data than strictly necessary for its function.
assumptions: The AI engine processes child data without adequate safeguards or if the data is more granular than needed.
uncertainty_note: Citation based on Dd.1.1 for explicit disclosure; context confirms DataStore->Process is valid interaction

title: Implicit data disclosure through AI processing
description: AI Recommendation Engine may derive additional personal information from child browsing data through pattern analysis, creating implicit disclosures beyond the original data collected.
assumptions: AI inference can extract sensitive attributes not explicitly present in browsing data.
uncertainty_note: Dd.1.2 for implicit disclosure; AI capabilities may vary

title: Lack of confidentiality in child data transfer
description: Child browsing data transferred to AI engine may be exposed to unauthorized parties during transmission or storage within the AI system.
assumptions: Data in transit or at rest in AI engine lacks adequate encryption or access controls.
uncertainty_note: L.1.1 for confidentiality at source/flow; standard threat for data transfers

title: Regulatory non-compliance for child data processing
description: Transferring child browsing data to AI engine may violate COPPA, GDPR-K, or other child privacy regulations requiring parental consent, data minimization, and limited retention.
assumptions: The system lacks proper consent mechanisms or data handling policies for minors.
uncertainty_note: Nc.1.1 for non-compliance; specific regulations depend on jurisdiction

title: AI engine may share child data with third parties
description: AI Recommendation Engine may transfer or share child browsing data with external vendors, analytics providers, or cloud services as part of its operation.
assumptions: AI engine has data sharing agreements or integrates with third-party services.
uncertainty_note: Dd.2.1 for disclosure to third parties; depends on AI engine architecture

title: Unintended consequences from AI profiling of children
description: AI Recommendation Engine may create behavioral profiles of children that lead to manipulative content recommendations, targeted advertising, or other harmful outcomes.
assumptions: AI algorithms optimize for engagement without considering child welfare.
uncertainty_note: U.1.1 for unintended consequences; AI behavior depends on implementation

title: Explicit Data Disclosure to Third-Party Advertisers
description: Browsing data is explicitly transferred from the AI Recommendation Engine to Third-Party Advertisers as part of the planned data flow. This represents an intentional disclosure of personal data across a system boundary.
assumptions: The data flow is designed to share browsing data with advertisers for targeted advertising purposes.
uncertainty_note: Tree node Dd.1.1 is inferred from context [5] on Data Disclosure methodology.

title: Linkability of Browsing Data with Advertiser Profiles
description: Third-Party Advertisers may link the received browsing data with other data sources they possess, creating a comprehensive user profile that exceeds the original purpose of the data transfer.
assumptions: Advertisers have access to additional data sources and can correlate browsing data with other identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Tree node L.1.1 is inferred from standard LINDDUN methodology for Process->ExternalEntity flows.

title: Identification of Users from Browsing Data
description: Browsing data transferred to advertisers may contain or enable identification of individual users, potentially revealing personal information beyond what was intended to be shared.
assumptions: Browsing data includes identifiers or quasi-identifiers that can be used to identify individuals.
uncertainty_note: Tree node I.1.1 is inferred from standard LINDDUN methodology for Process->ExternalEntity flows.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of stored government ID images
description: Government ID images stored in the file system could be accessed or disclosed to unauthorized parties through inadequate access controls, improper storage permissions, or data leakage mechanisms.
assumptions: The authentication service stores government ID images without sufficient access controls or encryption at rest.
uncertainty_note: Using Dd.1.1 as a reasonable threat-tree node for unauthorized data disclosure in Process→DataStore flows based on context [3] and [5].

title: Unauthorized access to stored government ID images
description: The authentication service may not properly restrict access to the file system where government ID images are stored, allowing unauthorized users or systems to access sensitive personal data.
assumptions: Access controls on the file system are insufficient or not properly enforced.
uncertainty_note: Using U.1.1 as a reasonable threat-tree node for unauthorized access in Process→DataStore flows.

title: Tampering with stored government ID images
description: Government ID images stored in the file system could be altered, corrupted, or tampered with during storage, compromising the integrity of the personal data.
assumptions: The file system lacks adequate integrity controls, checksums, or audit mechanisms to detect unauthorized modifications.
uncertainty_note: Using I.1.1 as a reasonable threat-tree node for data integrity threats in Process→DataStore flows.

title: Unavailability of stored government ID images
description: The authentication service may experience storage failures, system outages, or data loss that makes government ID images unavailable when needed.
assumptions: The file system lacks redundancy, backup mechanisms, or disaster recovery capabilities.
uncertainty_note: Using L.1.1 as a reasonable threat-tree node for data availability threats in Process→DataStore flows.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of JWT via localStorage
description: JWT tokens stored in browser localStorage are accessible to any JavaScript running on the page, including malicious scripts. This allows unauthorized disclosure of authentication credentials and user data to third parties.
assumptions: Browser has access to localStorage and no additional security controls (like HttpOnly cookies) are in place.
uncertainty_note: Tree node D.1.1 is a standard disclosure node; confidence in this classification is high based on localStorage security characteristics.

title: JWT Token Manipulation in localStorage
description: localStorage is fully accessible and modifiable by any JavaScript, allowing attackers to alter, forge, or tamper with stored JWT tokens. This enables session hijacking and privilege escalation.
assumptions: No integrity protection mechanisms (like cryptographic signing verification) are enforced at the application level.
uncertainty_note: Tree node Dd.1.1 is a standard data manipulation node; confidence is high given localStorage's inherent mutability.

title: Linkability of JWT to User Sessions
description: JWT tokens contain claims that can be used to link multiple sessions or activities to a single user, potentially enabling cross-session tracking and profiling.
assumptions: JWT payload contains identifiable user information or session identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Tree node L.1.1 is a standard linkability node; confidence depends on JWT payload structure which is not fully specified.

title: Identifiability of User via JWT Claims
description: JWT tokens typically contain user identifiers (sub, email, etc.) that can be extracted from localStorage, enabling direct identification of users without additional authentication.
assumptions: JWT payload includes standard user identification claims.
uncertainty_note: Tree node I.1.1 is a standard identifiability node; confidence depends on JWT payload structure.

title: Linking of child history data with other parent-accessible data
description: The parent user (EE1) reviewing child history (from P3) may be able to link this data with other data they have access to, potentially building a comprehensive profile of the child across multiple systems or contexts.
assumptions: Parent has access to other data sources that can be linked with child history
uncertainty_note: Using L.1.1 as a reasonable threat-tree node for linking scenarios

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child history to parent
description: Child history data may be disclosed to the parent user (EE1) beyond what is authorized or necessary, potentially revealing sensitive information about the child's medical, behavioral, or developmental history.
assumptions: Access controls may not properly restrict what child data is disclosed to parents
uncertainty_note: D.1.1 selected as appropriate disclosure threat node

title: Misinterpretation of child history data by parent
description: The parent user (EE1) may misunderstand or misinterpret the child history data retrieved from P3, leading to inappropriate conclusions or actions regarding the child's well-being or development.
assumptions: Parent may lack context or training to properly interpret child health/behavioral data
uncertainty_note: U.1.1 selected as appropriate understanding threat node
